thread.title_full: Bayelsa opens electricity market with first distribution licence

author: GuardianNigeria
title: Bayelsa opens electricity market with first distribution licence
text:
Bayelsa State has taken a major step towards establishing a locally regulated electricity market with the issuance of its first
with the issuance of its first Electricity Distribution Licence by the State Electricity Regulatory Agency . The regulatory agency, issued Electricity Distribution Licence No. BYERA/EDL/001 to Bayelsa Electricity Distribution Company Limited , marking the transition from regulatory preparation to actual market implementation in the state.
The licence was formally presented by the Director-General of BYERA, Dr RosaLyn Dressman, to the Managing Director of Port Harcourt Electricity Distribution Plc , Ete Pinnick, who received it on behalf of the group of companies. The 20-year licence authorises the licensee to undertake electricity distribution activities within its approved service area in Bayelsa State, subject to BYERA’s regulatory oversight, performance standards, consumer protection requirements and other conditions contained in the licence.
The development establishes a clearer regulatory framework for electricity distribution in the state, with BYERA expected to monitor operators, enforce service standards, protect consumers and promote investment in electricity infrastructure. For consumers, the new framework is expected to strengthen local oversight of critical areas including distribution performance, metering, billing, service standards, complaints handling and regulatory compliance.
It also provides a defined structure through which operators can be held accountable for the quality of electricity services delivered to households, businesses and communities across their approved service areas. The development is particularly significant as the licence is non-exclusive, meaning the issuance of the first distribution permit does not shut out other qualified investors or operators from participating in Bayelsa’s electricity market.
Subject to applicable laws, regulations and BYERA’s licensing requirements, other eligible participants may enter the market, a framework the agency said is intended to encourage investment, competition, innovation and improved service delivery. The approach is also designed to prevent the creation of a single gatekeeper for the state’s electricity market, while creating room for additional investment and operators to contribute to the expansion of electricity services.
The licensing milestone follows months of regulatory, technical and institutional work by BYERA to establish the rules, standards and processes required for electricity market participation in the state. With the issuance of the first licence, the regulatory framework moves beyond policy and preparation to implementation, with a licensed distribution operator, a defined regulatory authority and specific obligations governing electricity distribution now in place.
For BYERA, however, the licence marks the beginning of a broader regulatory responsibility rather than the conclusion of the reform process. The agency is expected to oversee operators, protect consumers, encourage investment and support the progressive strengthening of electricity infrastructure to meet the needs of Bayelsa’s communities and growing economy. Reliable electricity remains critical to businesses, industries, healthcare facilities, schools, public institutions and households, while improved power supply can also strengthen the state’s attractiveness to investors.
